RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is common in education and is not evidence of discrimination. Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of bias is legally groundless and would likely harm your professional standing.

While your administrative credentials may appear stronger on paper, senior appointments heavily weigh interview performance, institutional vision, stakeholder fit, and references. The appointed candidate also had substantial classroom experience and leadership coursework.

Do not bring up the panel’s gender. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your written debrief and scores against the selection criteria. Only if that feedback reveals demonstrable procedural breaches or biased criteria should you consider pursuing the matter through your union or legal counsel.
